findings.message: 10 eyebrow/kicker label(s) above headings: "EP.003" above "同桌认出我， 靠的是一句大实话。"; "The story, frame by frame" above "故事怎么发生。"; "Words from the story" above "五个词，五个故事瞬间。"; "我刚想说，我自——我自己讲。" above "05"; "故事第 2 格 ↗" above "actually"
findings.fix: Delete them. If the label carried real information, fold it into the headline or the supporting sentence.

findings.message: Monospace type outside code: ui-monospace — e.g. "EP.003", "01", "02", "03"
findings.fix: Set it in the text face. Monospace is for literal code inside <pre>/<code> only.
Remove them. If order truly matters, write it into the words ("First, …") or use a real <ol>.

findings.message: 11 tiny uppercase letter-spaced labels (e.g. "第一册 / UNIT 1 LIFE CHOICES", "Narration & subtitles", "The story, frame by frame", "Words from the story").
findings.fix: Use sentence-case text at a readable size, or delete the label.

findings.message: 1 box-shadow(s) on elements at rest: div.cover-paper → rgb(224, 230, 215) 8px 9px 0px 0px
findings.fix: Remove. Separate surfaces with a tone step or space. Shadows are for things that really float (menus, dialogs, sticky bars).

findings.message: 81 thin rule(s)/divider line(s): header.header 1440px | aside.language-note 1080px | div.word-strip 1080px | nav.contents 1080px
findings.fix: Delete. Separate with space, a tone change, or scale. Lines are only for real tables and form fields.
Define a surface by its fill (one tone step from the page) or leave the content unboxed.
Vary the composition; not every section is a card grid.

findings.message: Cream + terracotta palette (page background #f6f3eb, section #fffdf7, text #b84735).
findings.fix: Re-draw the palette from the library. This pairing reads as an assistant brand, not yours.
Darken or lighten the text colour.
A page needs about five: display, heading, lead, body, small.

findings.message: Only 2 picture(s) on the page (2 photographs, footage or raster images, 0 interface fragments). Drawings in SVG do not count.
findings.fix: Find real pictures of the subject's world with scripts/assets.mjs (photographs, archival images, maps, engravings, footage), download them to assets/ and give them room: a hero picture, one per section that has a subject, a full-width band. At least four, usually six to twelve.

findings.message: No video anywhere on the page.
findings.fix: Look for one honest clip with scripts/assets.mjs --video (the place, the material, the process) and use it as a muted loop with a poster frame. Defend its absence only if no clip fits the subject.

findings.message: Longest paragraph runs about 125 characters per line.

findings.fix: Nothing meant to be read goes below 13px.

findings.message: The first screen has no dominant element: the largest type is 58px (4vw) and no single picture holds a third of the viewport.
findings.fix: Make one thing lead: the headline at display size, or one large picture. A grid of many small pictures is not one thing; in blind tests jurors marked a first screen without a headline down every time. On the strongest studied sites the largest type has a median of 8.4vw.

findings.message: The sheet dealt Schibsted Grotesk and Schibsted Grotesk, but the page renders ui-sans-serif, ui-monospace.
findings.fix: Load the dealt face (the link on the sheet) and put it first in font-family. A build that falls back to a default face lands on the default look.

findings.message: The h1 is a bare name ("同桌认出我， 靠的是一句大实话。") and nothing else on the first screen says what this is.
findings.fix: Keep the name if it leads, and give the line under it (18px or more) the plain words: what it is, for whom, where or when. In the study of 97 Sites of the Day, first screens that named nothing lost usability and content points.

findings.message: Only 0 element(s) moved while the page loaded and scrolled.
findings.fix: Build the motion layer (SKILL.md step 9, references/motion.md): the signature move, an entrance for the parts of every section, feedback on every control, and one moving picture. Transform and opacity only, with a reduced-motion fallback.
